answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 30 keys loses far more than 30 single identities would. The karst graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the ocean audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the copper checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 3 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
